rows.what: Import graph vs a text-and-path baseline
rows.value: GitGalaxy found 84% of the baseline's 490 edges; 89% of its 463 edges are in the baseline
rows.detail: Baseline at the level of files: each include or import that names exactly one target in the repository (relative path first, then a unique match by trailing path; Go: the module path to a package directory; Rust: `mod x;`, `use crate::...` and other workspace crates). Edges only GitGalaxy has are usually includes it resolved among several same-named files (for example gitgalaxy/cobol_refractor_controller.py to gitgalaxy/tools/cobol_to_cobol/cobol_jcl_forge.py). No standing research rating exists yet for the import graph.

rows.what: Functions found vs a tree-sitter parse
rows.detail: 3,286 of 3,286 function definitions found by a plain parse are in the scan; 793 scan functions the parse did not find (macro-generated and renamed forms).

rows.what: Call edges found vs a tree-sitter name-matching baseline
rows.value: GitGalaxy found 53% of the baseline's 6,907 edges; 96% of its 3,810 edges are in the baseline
rows.detail: Baseline: each call to a name that exactly one function defines (or one in the same file) is an edge; calls through function pointers, fields and macros are not. GitGalaxy finds fewer of these plain calls because it keeps only edges that resolve to one definition. Treat hub lists, repair radius and call counts as lower bounds.
The same comparison at file level.

rating.label: Limited
rating.text: Consistency with a tree-sitter name matcher on this repository: Limited. (In our reference set this cheap check passed every C repository at 98 to 99% while compiler-grade recall ranged from 69% to 88%, so it does not predict the compiler-grade result.) Standing rating against a compiler-grade reference (pyan3), from our research on pinned python repositories: Fair. GitGalaxy's strict call edges had precision 53% and recall 65% there; a tree-sitter name matcher had recall 48%.

sentences: gitgalaxy-engine has 6,919 commits over 0.7 years (first 2026-03-21, latest 2026-11-20).
In the last 12 months: 6,919 commits by 15 authors, 22,144 function edits, 14 sweeps and 703 fix commits.

Today the code base has 4,079 functions in 295 files; main languages: python (217 files), java (54 files), markdown (13 files). The largest areas by functions are gitgalaxy/tools (2,574), gitgalaxy/core (1,142), gitgalaxy/recorders (108).
The median function is 0.1 years old (counted from the first scan 2026-03 (start) or its birth); 0% of today's functions were already there at the first scan.
The most-called function is __init__ (478 callers, gitgalaxy/core/detector.py); the most central is __init__ (gitgalaxy/core/detector.py). 4 of the top ten appear in both lists.
enforce_licensing_guard was once a hub (peak 22 callers in 2026-05); it is no longer in the code.
The most common function types are Stateful Encapsulated Methods (28%), Generic / Templated Code (18%), Encapsulated Accessors (14%).
By lines of code: python 88%, java 12%, cobol 0%. The biggest shift since the first scan: java went from 0% to 12%.
The largest function is record_mission (2,297 lines, gitgalaxy/recorders/record_keeper.py).
The most repaired function is _slice_by_braces (41 fix commits, gitgalaxy/core/detector.py).
Across its history 58% of function edits are organic change, 14% sweeps and 14% fixes; a fix arrives a median 10 days after the change that caused it.

Self-check of the call graph against a tree-sitter baseline on this repository: limited; import graph vs a text-and-path baseline: GitGalaxy found 84% of the baseline's 490 edges; 89% of its 463 edges are in the baseline; functions found vs a tree-sitter parse: recall 100%, precision 81%; call edges found vs a tree-sitter name-matching baseline: GitGalaxy found 53% of the baseline's 6,907 edges; 96% of its 3,810 edges are in the baseline.
